title: LuckRead Payment and Provider Event Inbox D1-04 Persistence Candidate

payments.purpose: Durable provider-backed payment attempt state and immutable request/commercial snapshot; not a ledger or entitlement store.

single_live_or_successful_attempt_per_or.invariant: An order cannot own two active or successful payment attempts; a new attempt is allowed after a terminal failure/cancel/expiry.

invariants: A Payment must reference an owned Order in CREATED/PENDING_PAYMENT with the same positive total and currency.
UNIQUE(customer_id, idempotency_key) scopes the payment creation key to a customer; key reuse for a different order/request conflicts.
Provider request runs outside a D1 transaction, using the same stable payment_id and idempotency_key on retries.
Provider resource.updated is monotonic; every stored mutation advances local version exactly once.
Terminal payment attempts are not reopened.
A partial unique index permits only one non-failed/non-cancelled/non-expired payment attempt per order; a confirmed successful payment cannot be double-charged by a second attempt.

payment_provider_events.purpose: Durable deduplication/reconciliation inbox for authenticated, signature-verified provider events; never raw event payload storage.
invariants: UNIQUE(provider, merchant_id, event_id) is the durable webhook deduplication key.
A duplicate event ID with the same payload hash is a replay; different payload hash requires reconciliation.
Raw webhook body, provider secret, client secret, card data, and entitlement information are never stored.

APPLIED and REJECTED receipts remain immutable. Only mandate_active/mandate_revoked receipts in RECONCILIATION_REQUIRED may be reopened to RECEIVED for exact same event ID and payload SHA after the local source payment/mandate is available; the immutable event identity cannot change.
When supplied in a signed mandate_details webhook, payment_id is retained as a safe local correlation field to bind the event to the exact setup payment; raw webhook body is never retained.
Refund lifecycle receipts may bind refund_id only when it matches the immutable local refund, payment, provider and merchant snapshot.
The refund_id event binding is immutable with the webhook receipt identity; unknown or mismatched refund resources are retained only as reconciliation/rejection evidence without applying the refund.

payment_provider_event_conflicts.purpose: Durable anomaly/reconciliation facts when an authenticated provider reuses an event ID with a different payload hash; the first verified receipt remains immutable.
invariants: Unique provider + merchant ID + event ID + incoming payload hash deduplicates repeated observation of the same conflict variant.
existing_payload_sha256 and incoming_payload_sha256 must differ; a same-hash replay belongs to the normal idempotent inbox path.
Occurrence count may advance by at most one per version-CAS update; last_seen_at cannot regress.
Resolution is explicit and terminal; resolved anomaly facts cannot be reopened or deleted.
No raw webhook body, API key, client secret or cardholder data is stored.
A conflict row can be inserted only when an immutable provider event receipt exists for the same provider, merchant, event ID, and existing payload hash.

revenuecat_webhook_events.purpose: Durable idempotent inbox for authenticated RevenueCat store-subscription lifecycle events. This is provider-event transport evidence only; RevenueCat's current subscriber API and LuckRead's immutable product-plan mapping are re-read before any subscription state change.

event_data_json.privacy: Allowlisted event fields only; subscriber_attributes and raw request body are excluded.

invariants: UNIQUE(app_id,event_id) is the RevenueCat webhook event identity within an explicitly allowlisted app.
Same event identity and same raw payload SHA-256 is an idempotent duplicate; same identity with a different hash creates a separate conflict fact.
Only the immutable original receipt is retained; raw webhook bytes and subscriber_attributes are never stored.
A durable receipt alone never creates a Payment, activates a Subscription, or grants a content entitlement.
Webhook event content is a hint for reconciliation; the current subscriber state must be read through RevenueCat's server API before applying subscription state.

revenuecat_webhook_event_conflicts.purpose: Durable anomaly facts when RevenueCat reuses an app/event ID with a different verified payload hash; the original webhook receipt remains immutable.
invariants: existing_payload_sha256 and incoming_payload_sha256 must differ.
Conflict can be recorded only when the referenced immutable first receipt exists for the same app_id, event_id, and original hash.
The same incoming conflict hash is stored once; later repeats advance occurrence_count and last_seen_at only.
Conflict records are retained and never deleted or reassigned.

refunds.purpose: Owner-scoped immutable refund request and provider lifecycle facts in D1-04. This is a financial reversal request/status record, not a Wallet/Ledger posting or entitlement authority.
invariants: A refund request is owner-scoped to the authenticated payment customer and the exact provider/merchant/payment snapshot.
A refund request can be reserved only for a Payment whose local status is succeeded; the provider rechecks actual captured amount at execution time.
Stable refund_id plus UNIQUE(customer_id,idempotency_key) prevents duplicate refund requests; semantic reuse with a different amount, payment, currency, merchant or reason conflicts.

INITIATING, pending, review and succeeded refunds reserve captured amount; failed refunds release their reservation. Concurrent reservations cannot exceed the locally captured-payment ceiling and Hyperswitch independently enforces amount_captured.
Refund amount, parent payment, owner, merchant, provider, currency and reason are immutable financial request facts; updates require version CAS and monotonic provider_updated_at.
Only a signature-verified refund_details webhook matching refund_id, payment_id, merchant_id, amount and currency may apply provider lifecycle state.
Unknown, stale, conflicting or mismatched events remain reconciliation/rejection evidence and do not change refund state.
A refund status never posts or reverses Ledger facts and never grants or revokes D1-01 subscription entitlements; those are separate future domain workflows.
Refund and event evidence is retained; raw webhook bodies, provider API keys, client secrets and card data are not stored.

migration.rule: Reviewed source only; no remote D1 mutation, Worker deployment or provider event application is authorized by this contract.

additionalCandidates.purpose: Additive RevenueCat webhook receipt and payload-conflict inbox; provider='hyperswitch' schema and provider constraints remain unchanged.
Additive owner-scoped refund reservations, provider lifecycle status, signed refund event binding and amount/CAS guards in the existing commerce database.

nonGoals: No new Worker, D1, Queue or Service Binding.
No raw webhook payload, client secret, API key, or card data persistence.
No cross-D1 foreign key or distributed transaction.
No provider event with the same event ID but a different payload hash can overwrite the first receipt; mismatch is recorded as a separate reconciliation conflict.
RevenueCat store receipts are not written to payment_provider_events, whose provider-specific schema remains authoritative only for Hyperswitch.
No RevenueCat entitlement is granted from the webhook payload; subscriber state re-read and W07 plan mapping resolution are a later reconciliation module.
No new Worker, D1, Queue, or Service Binding is introduced by the RevenueCat webhook inbox.
No refund ledger posting or compensation is implemented here; refund records are requests/provider facts only.
No subscription entitlement revocation or creator revenue adjustment is performed by refund persistence or webhook ingestion.
No new Worker, D1, Queue or Service Binding is introduced by the refunds migration.
promotionRule: Remain CONTRACTED_NOT_VERIFIED until exact migration/schema evidence, provider retry and webhook idempotency runtime tests, security negatives, and exact-commit Evidence Registry admission pass.
